findings.title: Telnet is open
findings.description: Telnet sends usernames, passwords and everything typed in plain text. Anyone on the network path can read them. Telnet on routers, switches and IoT devices is also a common target for botnets.
findings.evidence: TCP 23 accepted a connection; banner: Microsoft Windows XP telnetd
remediation: Disable the Telnet service on the device and use SSH instead.
Windows: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName TelnetServer (older systems).
Network gear (e.g. Cisco): 'line vty 0 15' → 'transport input ssh'.
If Telnet can't be disabled, restrict it to a management VLAN with firewall rules.

findings.title: SMB signing is not required
findings.description: Without mandatory SMB signing, an attacker on the local network can relay or tamper with file-sharing traffic (NTLM relay attacks). Domain controllers require signing by default; other servers often don't.
findings.evidence: SMB2 NEGOTIATE response SecurityMode: signing enabled, not required (dialect ?).
remediation: Group Policy › Computer Configuration › Windows Settings › Security Settings › Local Policies › Security Options:
"Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)" = Enabled.
Or per server (admin PowerShell): Set-SmbServerConfiguration -RequireSecuritySignature $true -Force
Samba: set 'server signing = mandatory' in smb.conf.
Run gpupdate /force, then rescan.
findings.statusNote: Sample: accepted until the device is replaced in Q1.

findings.title: SMBv1 is enabled
findings.description: The server still accepts SMB version 1, a 30-year-old file-sharing protocol with serious design flaws. Worms and ransomware such as WannaCry and NotPetya spread through SMBv1. Modern Windows, macOS and Linux clients don't need it.
findings.evidence: SMB1 NEGOTIATE offering only "NT LM 0.12" was accepted by the server.
remediation: Windows Server/PC (admin PowerShell): Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false -Force
Remove the feature completely: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol (restart required).
Across a domain: Group Policy › Computer Configuration › Administrative Templates › MS Security Guide › Configure SMBv1 server = Disabled.
NAS / Samba devices: set the minimum SMB protocol to SMB2 (Samba: 'server min protocol = SMB2_10').
Rescan this host to confirm the finding is resolved.

findings.title: CVE-2023-38408 in OpenSSH 8.2p1
findings.description: The PKCS#11 feature in ssh-agent in OpenSSH before 9.3p2 has an insufficiently trustworthy search path, leading to remote code execution if an agent is forwarded to an attacker-controlled system.
findings.evidence:
Detected: ssh (OpenSSH 8.2p1)
Banner: OpenSSH 8.2p1 Ubuntu 4ubuntu0.5 Ubuntu Linux; protocol 2.0
CPE: cpe:2.3:a:openbsd:openssh:8.2:p1:*:*:*:*:*:*
Version-based match: vendors sometimes back-port fixes without changing the version, so confirm against vendor advisories.
remediation: Update OpenSSH to a version that fixes CVE-2023-38408 (see the vendor advisory in the references).
If the vendor back-ported the fix, mark this finding as a false positive with a note.

findings.title: TLS 1.0 enabled
findings.description: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 were formally retired in 2021 (RFC 8996). They rely on weak hashing and are no longer accepted by modern browsers.
findings.evidence: Server accepted ClientHello for: TLS 1.0. Supported overall: TLS 1.0, TLS 1.2.
remediation: Allow only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.
Windows/IIS/RDP: disable old protocols and ciphers under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL, or use IIS Crypto / a hardening GPO, then restart.
Apache: SSLProtocol -all +TLSv1.2 +TLSv1.3 and SSLCipherSuite with modern AEAD suites.
nginx: ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; ssl_ciphers with ECDHE+AESGCM/CHACHA20 suites.
Appliances and printers: set the minimum TLS version in the device's web admin, and update its firmware if the option is missing.
Rescan to confirm.

findings.title: Weak TLS cipher suites accepted (RC4/3DES/DES)
findings.description: The server accepts outdated ciphers. RC4 has known biases and 3DES is vulnerable to the SWEET32 birthday attack.
remediation: Allow only AEAD suites with forward secrecy (ECDHE with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305).
Windows/IIS/RDP: disable old protocols and ciphers under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL, or use IIS Crypto / a hardening GPO, then restart.
Apache: SSLProtocol -all +TLSv1.2 +TLSv1.3 and SSLCipherSuite with modern AEAD suites.
nginx: ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; ssl_ciphers with ECDHE+AESGCM/CHACHA20 suites.
Appliances and printers: set the minimum TLS version in the device's web admin, and update its firmware if the option is missing.
